historical_anchor: Historical TF58 advanced the opening strike by one day after losing strategic surprise; on 11 Jun all four task groups launched a fighter sweep of about 208 F6F guided by radar-equipped TBM/SB2C aircraft against Saipan, Tinian and Guam.
Historical first-day US fighter loss was about 11 F6F, many to ground fire; Japanese air power in the Marianas was then progressively reduced through 14 Jun.

branch_force.note: The extra branch deck increases available sweep/reserve weight modestly rather than scaling the historical 208 sweep linearly; coordination/airspace saturation still bind.

execution.event: Launch opening sweep. No branch delay from the 3 Jun Seiran raid remains operationally meaningful.
First large fighter contacts over southern Marianas. Japanese strategic surprise is absent, but exact raid timing remains a tactical surprise.

Follow-on fighter-bomber/field suppression and shipping/installation attacks. US emphasis remains air superiority and airfield suppression rather than trying to destroy every dispersed aircraft on the ground.

US_loss_note: Most irreversible losses are F6F in air combat/AA plus a small operational component. Branch Japanese fixed-base C2 raises the price versus history, but does not overturn Hellcat numerical/quality advantage.
major_US_ship_damage: NONE on 11 Jun; no Japanese weapon-quality carrier track generates a coordinated anti-carrier strike.
end_of_day: TF58 holds local air superiority and continues the shaping campaign; no operational reason to break FORAGER schedule.
